files.why: Domain-free primitive exposing the current UI locale (reactive accessor, en fallback) that status labels and formatters read; no domain noun so it passes the shared/ structure test.
Composition root detects the user's language (e.g. navigator.language) and sets the locale once at startup.
Replace the raw `props.status` / "overdue" text with a locale-keyed label lookup for draft/issued/paid/void; invoice-status vocabulary is billing's, stays in-slice.
Replace the raw `appointment.status` text with a locale-keyed label lookup for scheduled/completed/cancelled; appointment-status vocabulary is scheduling's, stays in-slice.
This cross-slice app view renders a hardcoded English "overdue" invoice-status badge inline, which also needs localizing.

uncertain: Placement of the locale accessor: I put it in shared/lib (mirroring useDebounce.ts, and it carries no domain noun), but the initial value/detection is arguably an app/providers composition-root concern — split accessor (shared) vs wiring (app) may be debated.

Where the German status strings live: I assumed small locale-keyed Records inline in each slice component (matching the existing VARIANT_BY_STATUS pattern; the repo prefers duplication over premature abstraction). A per-slice labels module or a vue-i18n message catalog is the alternative and would change the file list.

ClientOverviewView's "overdue" badge: localizing it inline duplicates billing's label, but InvoiceStatusBadge is private (not in billing/index.ts) so the app view can't import it, and billing exposes no label helper. The clean fix might instead be exposing an invoice-status label via billing/index.ts — which would add/modify billing/index.ts and billing/ui.

Whether shared/lib/format.ts (dates and money hardcoded to en-US) is in scope: a real German launch usually needs localized dates/currency too, but the request names only statuses, so I left format.ts out of the file list.
questions: Is there an approved i18n approach — add vue-i18n (message catalogs), or a lightweight in-house locale map? This drives whether we create catalog/label files vs inline Records.
How is the user's language determined: browser (navigator.language), a user-profile setting, URL prefix, or an in-app language switcher (which would require reactive re-render + a persisted setting)?
Does 'display in the user's language' mean statuses only for now, or full localization including dates and currency (format.ts) as part of the German launch?
Is German being added alongside English with English as fallback, and are only these two locales in scope?
Can you confirm the German translations for each status (draft/issued/paid/void, scheduled/completed/cancelled) and the derived labels 'overdue' and 'Conflict'?
Are non-status UI strings (e.g. the 'Conflict' badge, section headings) explicitly out of scope for this request?
